label: copy phase: input v while outputting a repeated v (late positions)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase and only when the input token is v (100% of activations). About 85% of activations (89% of mass) come where the original sequence had a doubled v, so the model reads back the first v while it has to output the second v. Activity is concentrated at late recall positions (recall_idx >= 4, long sequences, L=9 holds 69% of mass), and it is near zero for L <= 4. Smaller misses are v inputs whose v appears again later (e.g. v y v). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase or on any other input token. Precision is low (~18%): most copy-phase v->v steps do not activate, and the false positives look the same as the hits, so the gating factor is not captured by these variables. Preceding k/2/h gives somewhat higher rates. Magnitude is larger at later t / larger L; I did not check other modulators.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=v (+3.65), prev_tok=k (+3.25), in_tok=v (+2.69), phase=2 & out_tok=v (+2.17), out_tok=v (+2.11), prev_tok=h (+1.68). Lower it: in_count=1 (-1.80), orig8=- (-1.69), next_out=f (-1.65), prev2_tok=v (-1.64).
